title: Man identified in shooting, other questions unanswered
article: More details are expected to be released today on the fatal shooting of a 39-year-old man after a confrontation with police in a Duncan trailer park.
Police have identified the man killed as Derek Welton, of Duncan.
Five RCMP officers came face to face with Welton who may have called 9-1-1 shortly after 6 p.m. Sunday while alone in his trailer at the Duncan RV Park and Campground on Boys Road.

Police say he had a knife in hand and refused to listen to a senior officer trying to calm him down inside the trailer. The officer shot Welton after other efforts to subdue him, including use of a Taser, failed.

Many questions surrounding the incident remain, including why Welton called 9-1-1, how many other officers were in the trailer with him, which officer discharged the taser, how big his knife was, details of his behaviour or actions before he was shot, and how many shots were fired.

Yesterday, police tape remained around the trailer. RCMP officers maintained control of the park's entrance but residents were free to come and go, said North Cowichan/Duncan RCMP spokesman Cpl. Darren Lagan. Investigators from the Vancouver Island Major Crime Unit and a forensic identification team were still on scene but are expected to vacate today following yesterday's autopsy, Lagan said.

The man's father, Carroll Welton, said he is waiting for answers as to why police used deadly force on the five-foot-eight, 150-pound man. He described his son as sometimes "erratic" and said police had to respond to his home for problems many times in the past three years.

Welton was addicted to prescription painkillers, which he started taking after a stint as a cleaning person at B.C. Hydro's Stave Falls visitor's centre, his father said. In a 2004 interview with the Cowichan Valley Citizen, Welton claimed his health was severely affected after he was forced to clean the building using a potentially lethal chemical called Hydro Seal.
Lagan said there is no evidence to suggest this was a suicide by cop incident but said investigators are not ruling anything out.

It is also too early in the investigation to conclude any wrongdoing from the senior officer who shot Welton, Lagan said. The officer has had 20 years of service with the RCMP and had responded to the trailer park to deal with Welton before, he said.
There will be a coroner's inquest, which is mandatory when someone is killed by police. - files from Canwest News Service
